concepts.name: The four regions of a two-set diagram
concepts.description: A two-set Venn diagram splits everything into only A, only B, both, and neither.

concepts.name: Solving for an unknown region
concepts.description: Once every other region and the total are known, the last region is found by subtraction.

concepts.name: The eight regions of a three-set diagram
concepts.description: Three overlapping circles create eight regions: three "only" regions, three "exactly two" regions, one "all three" region, and "none."

concepts.name: Reading survey word problems
concepts.description: Words like "both", "only", "at least one" and "neither" each point to a specific region or combination of regions.

concepts.name: Only A vs total in A
concepts.description: The total number of people "in A" includes everyone in the "only A" region plus everyone where A overlaps another circle.

formulas.title: Two-set regions
formulas.prompt: What are the four regions of a two-set Venn diagram?
formulas.formula:
Only A = |A| − |A∩B|
Only B = |B| − |A∩B|
Neither = Total − |A∪B|
formulas.explanation: The "both" region is |A∩B| itself; the other three regions are found by subtracting it out or subtracting the union from the total.
formulas.commonMistake: Confusing "only A" (a region) with the total size of A (a region plus the overlap).

formulas.title: The four regions add to the total
formulas.prompt: How are the four regions of a two-set Venn diagram related to the total?
formulas.formula: Total = Only A + Only B + Both + Neither
formulas.explanation: Knowing any three of the four quantities lets you find the fourth by subtraction.
formulas.example: Total=30, only A=12, only B=10, both=5: Neither = 30−12−10−5 = 3
formulas.commonMistake: Leaving out one of the four regions when solving for another.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A class of 30: 12 in only A, 10 in only B, 5 in both. How many are in neither?

formulas.title: Three-set regions
formulas.prompt: How many regions does a three-set Venn diagram have, and what are they?
formulas.formula: Only A, Only B, Only C, (A&B only), (B&C only), (A&C only), All three, None — 8 regions in total
formulas.explanation: Every element falls into exactly one of these eight non-overlapping regions.
formulas.example: Adding up all eight regions gives the total number of people surveyed
formulas.commonMistake: Confusing "A&B only" (exactly two) with |A∩B| (which also includes the all-three region).
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many distinct regions does a three-circle Venn diagram have?

formulas.title: Translating survey language
formulas.prompt: How do you translate phrases like "only", "both" and "neither" into Venn diagram regions?
formulas.formula:
"Only A" = the A region excluding all overlaps
"Both"/"all three" = the innermost shared region
"At least one" = everything except "none"
formulas.explanation: Getting these phrases right is usually the hardest part of a Venn diagram word problem — the arithmetic afterwards is simple.
formulas.example: "At least one of A or B" = Only A + Only B + Both
formulas.commonMistake: Treating "only A" and "total in A" as the same quantity.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Translate "at least one of A or B" into a sum of Venn diagram regions.

formulas.title: Only A vs total A
formulas.prompt: How does "only A" relate to the total count of A?
formulas.formula: Total in A = Only A + (A∩B only) + (A∩C only) + (all three)
formulas.explanation: The total count for a set includes every region touched by that circle, not just the part that does not overlap anything else.
formulas.example: If only A = 10 and A also overlaps B and C in various regions, the total for A is larger than 10
formulas.commonMistake: Reporting "only A" when the question asks for the total size of A, or vice versa.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Explain why "only A" is smaller than the total count of A whenever A overlaps another set.

formulas.title: Exactly two of three
formulas.prompt: Given the pairwise overlaps and the triple overlap, how many are in exactly two sets?
formulas.formula: Exactly two = (sum of the three pair overlaps) − 3 × (all three)
formulas.explanation: Each person in all three sets is counted in every pair overlap, three times in all.
formulas.example: Pairs 20, 15 and 10, all three 5: exactly two = 45 − 15 = 30.
formulas.commonMistake: Subtracting the triple overlap only once.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Pairs of 12, 9 and 7 and 3 in all three: how many are in exactly two?

levels.title: Reading the Regions
levels.description: A two-set Venn diagram always has exactly four non-overlapping regions.

blocks.title: Only A is not the same as all of A
blocks.body: If |A|=15 and 6 of those overlap with B, then "only A" — the part of A that does not touch B — is 15 − 6 = 9. The full circle for A is bigger than "only A" whenever there is any overlap.

blocks.title: The four regions
blocks.body: Only A, Only B, Both, Neither
blocks.caption: These four regions never overlap and always add up to the total.

blocks.body: Always double-check whether a question is asking for "only A" or for the full total of A — they are usually different numbers.

questions.question: In a two-set Venn diagram, |A|=15 and |A∩B|=6. What is "only A" (the part of A outside B)?
questions.method: Remove the overlapping part from the total for A.

questions.question: "Only A" in a two-set Venn diagram refers to

options.text: everyone in A, including any overlap with B
the part of A that does not overlap with B
everyone in either A or B
everyone outside both A and B

questions.explanation: "Only A" specifically excludes the part shared with B — it is |A| − |A∩B|.

hints.text: "Only A" is a strict subset of the full A region.

commonMistakes: Confusing "only A" with the full circle for A.

questions.question: A class of 30 students: 12 are in only A, 10 are in only B, and 5 are in both. How many are in neither?

figure.caption: The class of 30
figure.ariaSummary: Two overlapping circles A and B in a class of 30: only A is 12, only B is 10, both is 5, and the region outside both is unknown.

questions.explanation: Total = Only A + Only B + Both + Neither, so 30 = 12 + 10 + 5 + Neither, giving Neither = 3.
questions.method: The four regions must add up to the total.

hints.text: Add the three known regions, then subtract from the total.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to include one of the three known regions.

questions.question: If |A|=20, |B|=15 and |A∩B|=8, what is "only B"?
questions.method: Remove the shared region from the total for B.

hints.text: Use the total for B, not for A.

commonMistakes: Using |A| instead of |B| in the subtraction.

questions.question: In a two-set Venn diagram, "only A" = 14 and "both" = 6. What is the total count of A (|A|)?
questions.method: The total for a set includes its "only" region plus any overlap.

hints.text: |A| is bigger than "only A" whenever there is overlap.

commonMistakes: Reporting "only A" (14) as the total for A.

questions.question: A survey of 50 students: 20 play only cricket, 15 play only football, and 8 play both. How many play at least one of the two sports?

figure.caption: The survey of 50 students
figure.ariaSummary: Two overlapping circles, Cricket and Football, among 50 students: only cricket is 20, only football is 15 and both is 8.

questions.explanation: "At least one" = Only cricket + Only football + Both = 20 + 15 + 8 = 43.
questions.method: "At least one" adds up every region except "neither."

hints.text: Sum every region that is not "neither."

questions.question: Continuing the previous survey of 50 students, where 43 play at least one sport, how many play neither?
questions.method: "Neither" is the total minus everyone accounted for.

hints.text: Subtract the "at least one" count from the total.

commonMistakes: Subtracting only one of the "only" regions instead of the full "at least one" count.

questions.question: |A| (the total for A) is 25, and "only A" is 18. What is |A∩B|?
questions.method: The overlap makes up the difference between the total and "only."
commonMistakes: Confusing this with a subtraction involving |B| instead.

questions.question: Only A = 10, Only B = 14, Neither = 6, and the total is 40. How many are in both A and B?

figure.caption: A group of 40
figure.ariaSummary: Two overlapping circles A and B in a group of 40: only A is 10, only B is 14, neither is 6, and the overlap is unknown.

questions.explanation: Total = Only A + Only B + Both + Neither, so 40 = 10 + 14 + Both + 6, giving Both = 10.
questions.method: Rearrange the total equation to isolate the unknown region.

hints.text: Add up the three known regions, then subtract from the total.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to include "neither" among the known regions.

questions.question: How many distinct, non-overlapping regions does a three-circle Venn diagram have (including "none")?
questions.explanation: Three circles create 3 "only" regions, 3 "exactly two" regions, 1 "all three" region, and 1 "none" region: 3+3+1+1 = 8.
questions.method: Count each type of region separately, then add them up.

hints.text: Do not forget the region outside all three circles.

questions.question: In a survey of 100: only A=30, only B=25, only C=20, (A&B only)=8, (B&C only)=5, (A&C only)=4, all three=3. How many are in none of the three?

figure.caption: The survey of 100
figure.ariaSummary: Three overlapping circles A, B and C in a survey of 100, with every region counted except the region outside all three, which is unknown.

questions.explanation: Sum of the seven known regions: 30+25+20+8+5+4+3 = 95. None = 100 − 95 = 5.
questions.method: Add up every known region, then subtract from the total.

hints.text: There are seven regions besides "none" — make sure to add all of them.

commonMistakes: Missing one of the "exactly two" regions in the sum.

questions.question: A total of 100 people were surveyed. 70 like at least one of A or B. |A|=45 and |B|=40. What is |A∩B|?
questions.method: Use the union formula, rearranged to isolate the overlap.

hints.text: "At least one" is the same as the union.

commonMistakes: Confusing "at least one" with the total surveyed.

questions.question: Of 70 people: only A=15, only B=12, only C=10, exactly two of the three (combined, all pairs)=18, and all three=5. How many are in none of the three?
questions.method: Add every known region (grouping the "exactly two" regions together here), then subtract from the total.

hints.text: The "exactly two" total already combines all three pairwise-only regions.

commonMistakes: Double-counting the "exactly two" regions by also trying to split them further.
